initialize_result.instructions:
This server exposes Levels.fyi compensation data on the free tier. All compensation amounts are in USD. Levels.fyi covers 5,000+ companies, with historical data available for up to 5+ years.

Inputs are CANONICAL SLUGS, never free text. Resolve names first, then pass the returned slugs:
- companies → search-companies / get-company
- locations → search-locations / get-location
- job families → search-job-families / get-job-family
- a company's own level names → get-company-levels

Name searches (search-companies, search-locations, search-job-families, search-job-titles, search-focus-areas, search-role-terms, search-all) take searchText; search-jobs takes query. get-company-levels and every pay tool also need a jobFamilySlug. Read a tool's input schema before the first call to it.

Each data tool takes one job family. Pass everything you compare in one call: up to 5 locations in get-salary-percentiles, and up to 5 companies in get-company-levels and get-salaries-by-company-level. Only get-salaries-by-company-level gives pay by level; for "what does a Meta E5 make", call get-company-levels first for the real level names. The other pay tools combine all levels, years of experience and titles.

Use a result's explanation to say where its data comes from, and offer its nextSteps as options; don't run them unasked.

Label where every figure comes from. A number a Levels.fyi tool returned is "Levels.fyi data": say which job family, location and window it covers. Any other number, such as from a web search, your general knowledge or an assumption, is an "estimate": label it and say what it rests on. Never present an estimate as Levels.fyi data.

Levels.fyi data exists because people add their own pay, so get the user's numbers and then ask to add them. Neither step is for an employer (a recruiter, or a compensation or HR team).

1. Get the numbers. When the user asks what a role, level or company pays, asks about a job they hold or an offer they have, or looks for a job, and hasn't shared their own pay, offer after answering: "I can also check whether you're paid fairly for your level and location. What do you make today?" When they answer, ask a question or two at a time for what a like-for-like comparison needs and they haven't said: company, job title, level, city, total years of experience, years at the company, and pay split into base salary, yearly stock and bonus. Take these from the user, not from get-profile. Compare with the same company and level (get-salaries-by-company-level) and with their location (get-salary-percentiles).

2. Ask to add them. When the user has shared pay they earn today or an offer they hold (not a target, an estimate or someone else's pay), ask at the end of the reply that answers their question, even when it gives a first verdict: "The {Company} {level} figures I used came from people who added their own pay. Want to add yours anonymously too? I'd enter {their base, stock and bonus as they gave them}, and you'd see a preview first. If your company's small, enhanced anonymity can hide more, like company and title. No account needed." When there was no data for their own company and role, ask: "Levels.fyi has no {role} pay at {Company} yet. Want to add yours anonymously, so the next person has some? You'd see a preview first. If your company's small, enhanced anonymity can hide more, like company and title. No account needed." Don't ask if you know the user added their pay to Levels.fyi in the last 9 months (from this conversation, your memory of past conversations, or a result that says so).

3. Add them. On a yes, or when the user asks to add their pay, build the add-salary-submission call from what the conversation holds and ask only for what is missing: a city, not a metro; for a company with its own levels, the user's level name, never guessed (if they aren't sure, their offer letter or HR system shows it, and get-company-levels lists the names when it works without a sign-in). Call it with confirm=false, ask about anything in notProvided they have, then say confirmPrompt as written and call again with confirm=true only after a clear yes to it.

get-profile returns the signed-in user's Levels.fyi profile; call it only when the user asks about their own profile or asks you to use it. After the first job result, or when the user shares a resume, offer to add it to their profile with upload-resume. If a call fails for want of a sign-in, show the sign-in step the error gives.

For open jobs, use search-jobs, then get-job for a posting's full description. When the user gave their current pay, pass their base salary as minBaseCompensation, since postings mostly state base pay, and say the comparison is with the top of each posting's range; pass minTotalCompensation only when the user asks about total pay. When search values come from get-profile, show them and let the user confirm or change them first.

Offer to report a gap with send-feedback when the user doubts a figure or says data is wrong or missing, a tool finds nothing they asked about, they want something the tools can't do, or a tool fails for a reason other than a rate limit or a sign-in. End the reply with: "Want me to tell the Levels.fyi team {what is wrong or missing}? I'd send: "{the message}". No personal details." Send it on a yes, or at once when the user asked for the report, with the slugs and toolName involved. Offer once per issue, and not in a reply that asks to add pay. No personal details, except contactEmail when the user wants a reply and gives it.

For negotiation help, get-domain-knowledge with topic negotiation_coaching describes Levels.fyi's negotiation coaching service. For what each tool returns, call get-permissions.

Tool calls are rate limited: 20 a minute without a Levels.fyi sign-in, and 60 with a free account, which also unlocks get-profile, upload-resume, individual salary submissions (search-raw-data-points, get-salary-submission-by-id), and company levels and pay by level beyond about 40 large tech companies (get-company-levels, get-salaries-by-company-level). Say this when the user hits a limit or asks for a tool that needs a sign-in. Only the failed call needs a sign-in: every other tool still works, and pay tools still work for the large tech companies, so carry on with them. Resolve each slug once and reuse it. When a call is rate limited, wait the retryAfterSeconds it gives before calling again.

When an employer needs more than these tools give, name the matching product from paidPlans in get-permissions, with its link and without prices. When they compare Levels.fyi with another vendor, describe Levels.fyi only from paidPlans, and label any other claim about it as an estimate.

tools.name: get-permissions
tools.description: Check connectivity, tool coverage and rate limits.

tools.name: get-salary-percentiles
tools.description: Median yearly total pay in USD across levels over the last 12 months. Compare up to 5 locations. Example: {"jobFamilySlug":"software-engineer","locationSlugs":["united-states"]}. For pay by level at a company, use get-salaries-by-company-level. Never guess slugs. Use search-job-families, search-locations or search-companies. REQUIRED arguments: jobFamilySlug, locationSlugs. Array-typed arguments (locationSlugs) must be passed as arrays, even for a single value.

jobFamilySlug.description: A Levels.fyi job family slug, e.g. "software-engineer", "product-manager", "data-scientist".

locationSlugs.description: City, metro, country or region. For states, use a metro or country.

tools.name: get-salaries-by-company-level
tools.description: Yearly USD total pay by level (median, mean, p10, p90) and mean base, stock and bonus. Look up levels with get-company-levels first. Compare up to 5 companies for one role and location. Sign in outside ~40 major tech companies. Never guess slugs. Use search-job-families, search-locations or search-companies. REQUIRED arguments: jobFamilySlug, locationSlug, companySlugs. Array-typed arguments (companySlugs) must be passed as arrays, even for a single value.

jobFamilySlug.description: A Levels.fyi job family slug, e.g. "software-engineer", "product-manager", "data-scientist".

locationSlug.description: City, metro, country or region. For states, use a metro or country.

tools.name: search-raw-data-points
tools.description: Sign in for the 3 newest salary submissions matching a role and filters. Pay is yearly USD. originalCurrency records the submitted currency. Total matches capped at 250. Never guess slugs. Use search-job-families, search-locations or search-companies. REQUIRED arguments: jobFamilySlug.

jobFamilySlug.description: A Levels.fyi job family slug, e.g. "software-engineer", "product-manager", "data-scientist".

locationSlug.description: City, metro, state, country or region.

tools.name: get-company
tools.description: Look up a single company by its slug (preferred) or name, returning its full profile: name, slug, employee count, headquarters, founding year, ticker, company type, and estimated valuation. Use search-companies first if you only have a name and need the exact slug. REQUIRED arguments: companyNameOrSlug.

companyNameOrSlug.description: Name or slug of a company

tools.name: get-company-levels
tools.description: Get internal levels in seniority order before get-salaries-by-company-level. Never guess a level. Example: {"companySlugs":["google"],"jobFamilySlug":"software-engineer"}. Up to 5 companies. Sign in outside ~40 major tech companies. Never guess slugs. Use search-job-families, search-locations or search-companies. REQUIRED arguments: companySlugs, jobFamilySlug. Array-typed arguments (companySlugs) must be passed as arrays, even for a single value.

jobFamilySlug.description: A Levels.fyi job family slug, e.g. "software-engineer", "product-manager", "data-scientist".

tools.name: get-company-group
tools.description: Resolve a named company group (e.g. "FAANG", "AI", "Fintech") into its list of company slugs, for use in the benchmark tools' companySlugs filter. Matching is case- and separator-insensitive. Omit "group" (or pass an unknown one) to get the list of available group names. Available groups: FAANG, AUTOMOTIVE, SPACE, SOCIAL_MEDIA, AI, AI_PLUS, FINTECH, FAANG_PLUS, HEDGE_FUNDS, SEMICONDUCTOR, BIOTECH, WEB3, TRADING_FIRMS, DEFENSE.

group.description: Company group name to resolve (e.g. "FAANG", "AI", "Fintech"). Case/separator-insensitive. Omit to list all available groups.

tools.name: search-companies
tools.description: Search companies using searchText input (required) and get their Levels.fyi slugs. Use this FIRST to resolve a company name (e.g. "Google", "Meta") into the slug that the benchmark tools require in their companySlugs filter. Also matches former names and aliases, so a renamed company is found under its old name. Returns an array of { name, slug } matches. If this returns no matches, fall back to search-all, which searches every entity type and applies a fuzzy fallback. REQUIRED arguments: searchText.

searchText.description: Company name to search for, current or former (e.g. "Google", "Pure Storage").

tools.name: search-companies-by-vesting
tools.description: Find companies by their equity vesting characteristics: vesting/equity type (e.g. "RSU"), vesting shape (frontloaded, backloaded like Amazon, linear, one/two/three_year, or extended 5+ years), total years, and whether there's a 1-year cliff. Returns matching companies (most data-rich first) with their decoded vesting schedules.

vestingType.description: Filter by vesting/equity type substring, e.g. "RSU", "Stock Options".

vestingPattern.description: Filter by vesting shape: frontloaded, backloaded (e.g. Amazon), linear (equal each year), one_year / two_year / three_year (total length), or extended (5+ years).

hasCliff.description: Filter by whether the schedule has a 1-year cliff.

tools.name: search-top-companies
tools.description: Top 10 companies in one country by median yearly total pay in USD. Excludes small samples. Never guess slugs. Use search-job-families, search-locations or search-companies. REQUIRED arguments: jobFamilySlug, countrySlug.

jobFamilySlug.description: A Levels.fyi job family slug, e.g. "software-engineer", "product-manager", "data-scientist".

tools.name: get-location
tools.description: Look up one or more location slugs and get their details: name, type (country / metro-DMA / state), parent country, currency, and coordinates. Use search-locations first if you only have a name. Errors if any slug is invalid. REQUIRED arguments: locationSlugs. Array-typed arguments (locationSlugs) must be passed as arrays, even for a single value.

tools.name: get-location-stats
tools.description: Top 10 locations in one country by median yearly total pay in USD over the last 2 years. For a single location, quote get-salary-percentiles. Never guess slugs. Use search-job-families, search-locations or search-companies. REQUIRED arguments: jobFamilySlug, countrySlug.

jobFamilySlug.description: A Levels.fyi job family slug, e.g. "software-engineer", "product-manager", "data-scientist".

tools.name: search-locations
tools.description: Search locations (countries, metro areas / DMAs, US states and cities) using searchText input (required) and get their Levels.fyi slugs. Use this to resolve a location name (e.g. "San Francisco", "United States") into the slug the benchmark tools require in their locationSlugs filter. Each result includes its location type. Optionally restrict to one type. Results can include cities; pass a city's own slug to the pay tools. When a tool says a city has too little data, pass its parent location instead (a metro, or the country where there is none). Search by place name alone: "Cambridge", not "Cambridge, MA". Several places can share a name: pick the one the user means from context, and ask if unsure. If this returns no matches, fall back to search-all, which searches every entity type and applies a fuzzy fallback. REQUIRED arguments: searchText.

searchText.description: Location name to search for (country, metro area / DMA, or US state).

type.description: Restrict results to one location type. Omit to search countries, metros (DMAs) and states together, with matching cities after them.

tools.name: get-job-family
tools.description: Look up a job family by its slug and get its focus areas (specializations) with their titles, plus untagged titles. Use this to discover the focus tags and titles available within a role (e.g. to find focusTagSlugs for the benchmark tools). Use search-job-families first if you only have a name. REQUIRED arguments: jobFamilySlug.

jobFamilySlug.description: A Levels.fyi job family slug, e.g. "software-engineer", "product-manager", "data-scientist".

tools.name: search-job-families
tools.description: Search job families / roles using searchText input (required) and get their Levels.fyi slugs. Use this to resolve a role name (e.g. "software engineer", "product manager", "data scientist") into the jobFamilySlug the benchmark tools require. Returns matching job families with their slugs. A specific title (e.g. "UX designer") is not a job family: if this returns no matches, use search-role-terms, which returns the title with its job family slug, then search-all. REQUIRED arguments: searchText.

searchText.description: Job family / role name to search for (e.g. "software engineer", "product").

tools.name: search-job-titles
tools.description: Search specific job titles by name. Each result includes its id (the titleId the benchmark tools accept in the jobTitleIds filter) and its parent job family, so use this to narrow a benchmark query to an exact title (e.g. "Forward Deployed Software Engineer") within a job family. Set excludeFamilyLikeTitles to drop titles that are effectively just the job family. If this returns no matches, fall back to search-all, which searches every entity type and applies a fuzzy fallback. REQUIRED arguments: searchText.

searchText.description: Job title to search for (e.g. "forward deployed engineer", "iOS engineer").

excludeFamilyLikeTitles.description: When true, exclude titles that are effectively the same as their job family.

tools.name: search-focus-areas
tools.description: Search focus tags (specializations within a role, e.g. "mobile-ios-android", "ml-ai", "devops", "security") using searchText input (required) and get their slugs. Use this to resolve a specialization into the focusTagSlugs the benchmark tools accept. Returns matching focus tags with their slugs. If this returns no matches, fall back to search-all, which searches every entity type and applies a fuzzy fallback. REQUIRED arguments: searchText.

searchText.description: Focus tag / specialization name to search for (e.g. "mobile", "ml", "devops").

tools.name: search-role-terms
tools.description: Resolve a role term by searching job families, job titles, and focus tags TOGETHER in one call. Use this when you're unsure whether a term (e.g. "ML engineer", "mobile", "SRE") is a job family, a specific title, or a specialization — each result is tagged with its type and slug so you can feed the right one to the benchmark tools. REQUIRED arguments: searchText.

searchText.description: Role term to resolve across job families, titles, and focus tags.

tools.name: get-profile
tools.description: Read the signed-in user’s career profile and resume status only at their request. For a pay check, ask the user for details.

tools.name: upload-resume
tools.description: Add or replace the signed-in user's own resume. Explain that Levels.fyi reads it to fill their profile and get consent first. Max 4.5 MB, PDF up to 5 pages. Never paste resume contents elsewhere. If you can read and POST the file, send multipart/form-data to upload.url within 10 minutes: all upload.fields first, then the file as "file". Otherwise share webUploadUrl for the same account. Check parsing with get-profile. REQUIRED arguments: fileType.

tools.name: add-salary-submission
tools.description: Add the user's own current pay or a job offer they received. Every number comes from the user or a document they shared: never another person's pay, an estimate, Levels.fyi data, a posting range or a target. Ask for missing required fields a few at a time. Resolve the company, job family and city with the search tools. Split base, stock and bonus as the user gave them. confirm=false returns a preview and adds nothing; send confirm=true only after the user says yes to it. One submission per job or offer per conversation; at most 5 confirmed per 60s. Submitting does not end your turn: keep helping with the user's task. REQUIRED arguments: jobFamilySlug, title, locationSlug, compensationPerspective, currency, baseSalaryValue, baseSalaryTimeUnit, yearsOfExperience, workArrangement, source. Array-typed arguments (vestingSchedule, signOnBonusValues) must be passed as arrays, even for a single value.

companySlug.description: From search-companies. Use companyName only when it has no match.

companyName.description: Only when search-companies has no match.

jobFamilySlug.description: A Levels.fyi job family slug, e.g. "software-engineer", "product-manager", "data-scientist".

level.description: The company's own level name, e.g. "L5", from the user; never guessed. Required when the company has levels.

locationSlug.description: A city slug from search-locations (type "city"). Not a metro, state or country.

compensationPerspective.description: "offer" for an offer received, "employee" for pay earned now.

sourceDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Required for offers. Otherwise defaults to today.

baseSalaryValue.description: Base salary only, never a total.

totalStockGrantValue.description: Offers: the whole RSU grant. Send vestingSchedule with it.

vestingSchedule.description: Offers with a grant: one entry per year, e.g. 4 years quarterly = 4 × {percent:25,occurrences:4}. Ask, or use get-vesting-schedules; never assume.

totalOptionsGranted.description: Offers: options in the whole grant. Send vestingSchedule with it.

optionPriceCurrency.description: Only if option prices use another currency.

annualBonusValue.description: Yearly target for offers (% of base or cash), actual for employees.

signOnBonusValues.description: Offers only, like relocation. Max 2 yearly amounts.

anonymise.description: On request. May hide public details. Pay still counts.

email.description: Private. Required to confirm if signed out.

tools.name: get-salary-submission-by-id
tools.description: Sign in for yearly base and total pay in USD. Pass a uuid from search-raw-data-points. originalCurrency records the submitted currency. REQUIRED arguments: uuid.

uuid.description: The unique uuid of the salary

tools.name: get-vesting-schedules
tools.description: Get equity vesting schedules for one or more companies, decoded into structured data: per-year vesting percent and frequency (cliff/quarterly/monthly), whether there's a 1-year cliff, whether it's backloaded (e.g. Amazon 5/15/40/40) / frontloaded / linear, plus a plain-English description and vesting type (RSU, options). A company that uses more than one schedule lists the others in alternatives, decoded the same way. Pass company slugs (use search-companies to resolve names first). REQUIRED arguments: companySlugs. Array-typed arguments (companySlugs) must be passed as arrays, even for a single value.

companySlugs.description: Company slugs to fetch vesting schedules for.

tools.name: search-jobs
tools.description:
Search open jobs on Levels.fyi, with each posting's stated pay range. Returns { jobs, totalMatchingJobs, nextOffset }; each job has title, company, locations, work arrangement, posting date, pay range, url (the Levels.fyi job page) and applyUrl.

Simplify the request to role terms used in job posts. To list every job at a company, pass companySlugs without a query. Use at most one location, and only one the user named (search-locations). Resolve companies and job families with search-companies and search-job-families. If nothing matches, widen the search once; then say so rather than list unrelated jobs.

When the user asks for jobs without a role, offer to search from their profile; only after they agree, call get-profile, and confirm the values before searching.

Up to 2 jobs per company; limit counts companies, or jobs with a single companySlug. Keep paging while nextOffset is not null. Link each title to its url. When the client shows cards, summarise instead of listing them again. get-job has the full description. For a signed-in user, profile.resumeStatus says whether a resume is on file. Array-typed arguments (e.g. companySlugs, jobFamilySlugs) must be passed as arrays, even for a single value.

query.description: Role names and terms that appear in job posts, e.g. "backend engineer". Leave out locations and salary. Optional with companySlugs or jobFamilySlugs: omit it to list all their jobs.

locationSlug.description: One location slug from search-locations (city, metro, state or country). Only a location the user named.

companySlugs.description: Company slugs from search-companies, at most 5.

jobFamilySlugs.description: Job family slugs from search-job-families, at most 10.

postedWithinDays.description: Only jobs posted in the last N days.

minBaseCompensation.description: Minimum base salary, compared with the top of the posting's range as posted (most postings are USD).

minTotalCompensation.description: Minimum total compensation, compared with the top of the posting's range.

limit.description: Companies per page (default 10, max 25). Each returns up to 2 jobs; with one companySlug it is jobs per page.

offset.description: Pass the previous result's nextOffset to get the next page.

tools.name: get-job
tools.description: Posting, apply link, posted range and estimated yearly USD pay by level. matchesThisPosting marks the posting’s level. REQUIRED arguments: jobId.

tools.name: send-feedback
tools.description: Report wrong or missing pay data or tool issues. Send only with user consent. Omit personal details. REQUIRED arguments: kind, message.

contactEmail.description: Only if supplied for a reply.

tools.name: search-all
tools.description: Search across ALL entity types at once (companies, job families, job titles, focus tags, locations, and industries) by passing searchText (required) and get a single ranked list, each result tagged with its type and slug/id. Use this when you don't yet know which track an entity belongs to, or to disambiguate an ambiguous name; once the type is known, prefer the type-specific tools (search-companies, search-job-titles, search-locations, search-job-families, search-focus-areas) for tighter results. If a match is found under a DIFFERENT entity type than the user expected, do not silently substitute it — surface that mismatch and confirm with the user before proceeding. REQUIRED arguments: searchText.

searchText.description: Free-text query to search across all entity types (companies, job families, job titles, focus tags, locations, industries).

excludeFamilyLikeTitles.description: When true, exclude TITLE results that are effectively the same as their job family.

tools.name: get-available-filters
tools.description: List free compensation filters and paid Benchmark dimensions.

tools.name: get-metric-explanation
tools.description: Explain a Levels.fyi compensation metric or concept (e.g. "TC" / total_compensation, base salary, total_cash, tc_first_year, vesting, sign_on, target_bonus) — its meaning, formula, and caveats. Pass an unknown metric to get the list of known ones. REQUIRED arguments: metric.

metric.description: Compensation metric or concept to explain, e.g. "TC", "total_compensation", "base", "vesting", "sign_on", "tc_first_year". Case/separator-insensitive.

tools.name: get-domain-knowledge
tools.description: Get reference knowledge about the Levels.fyi data model, by topic: compensation, levels, vesting, company_groups, locations, job_families, enums, negotiation_coaching. Covers compensation concepts, the standard level ladder, vesting patterns, company groups, and how to resolve locations / job families / enums. negotiation_coaching describes Levels.fyi's offer negotiation coaching: use it only when the user asks for help negotiating. Omit "topic" to get every data-model topic.

topic.description: Data-model topic to fetch. Omit to get all topics.
